builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Rethinking LoRA Initialization for Robust Asymmetric Learning Rates
summary: It replaces the standard LoRA initialization (A drawn at conventional scale, B zero) with an A variance scaled as 1/n^2 while keeping B0=0, so LoRA+ asymmetric learning rates remain stable at high eta_B/eta_A ratios. The cost is negligible: a one-line change to the initialization scale with no added memory, latency, or training time, though it presumes LoRA+ asymmetric LRs are in use. It can fail to matter when LoRA+ is not used, when a small LR ratio is already adequate, or when the width-based guideline eta_B approximately n*eta_A does not transfer to the specific model and task, so per-task validation is still required.
rationale: For an engineer fine-tuning with LoRA on a single 24 GB GPU, this is a near-zero-cost initialization change that reduces learning-rate tuning brittleness, but its benefits depend on the specific LoRA+ setup and must be validated on the reader's workload.

claims.statement: It replaces the standard LoRA initialization (A drawn at conventional scale, B zero) with an A variance scaled as 1/n^2 while keeping B0=0, so LoRA+ asymmetric learning rates remain stable at high eta_B/eta_A ratios. The cost is negligible: a one-line change to the initialization scale with no added memory, latency, or training time, though it presumes LoRA+ asymmetric LRs are in use. It can fail to matter when LoRA+ is not used, when a small LR ratio is already adequate, or when the width-based guideline eta_B approximately n*eta_A does not transfer to the specific model and task, so per-task validation is still required.
Reduces initialization-noise energy by an additional factor of 1/n, substantially widening the stable learning-rate region and preventing high-ratio performance collapse in LoRA+ training.
